## Stretch Questions

__Reproduce the chart Elliot using the data from the names_year.csv file. If, after a couple of hours, you can get the chart close, but not exactly the same, that is okay. You will learn more to the degree you push yourself.__

```{python}
elliot_over_time = df.filter((pl.col("name").str.to_lowercase() == "elliot") & (pl.col("year") >= 1950))

max_total = elliot_over_time["Total"].max()
(
    ggplot(elliot_over_time, aes(x="year", y="Total", color="name"))
    + scale_x_continuous(breaks=[1950, 1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020], format="d")
    + geom_vline(xintercept=1982, color="red", linetype="dashed")
    + geom_text(x=1981.5, y=max_total, color="grey", label="E.T. Released", hjust=1,size=5)
    + geom_vline(xintercept=1985, color="red", linetype="dashed")
    + geom_text(x=1985.5, y=max_total, color="grey", label="Second Release", hjust=0,size=5)
    + geom_vline(xintercept=2002, color="red", linetype="dashed")
    + geom_text(x=2002.5, y=max_total, color="grey", label="Third Release", hjust=0,size=5)
    + geom_line()
    + scale_color_manual(
        values={"Elliot": "blue"},
        name="Name"
    )
    + labs(
        title="Elliot...What?",
        x="Year",
        y=""
    )
)
```
